scenes.title: From source to findings
scenes.narration: Deslop parses your source code with tree-sitter, finds candidate copies, checks their content, and groups the surviving findings. The CLI, editor and MCP tools all share the same Rust engine, so every surface reports the same result. It supports C, C#, Rust, Python, Dart, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, F#, Go and Osprey. It respects dot-gitignore and skips dependency trees and build artifacts by default.
scenes.excerpt: Deslop parses source code with tree-sitter, finds candidate copies, checks their content, and groups the surviving findings.

scenes.title: Normalization and candidate checks
scenes.narration: The engine normalizes syntax trees, so renamed variables, changed literals or reformatted code do not hide candidates. It fingerprints whole subtrees and consecutive statement runs, including copies inside a single file, and uses structural overlap and MinHash similarity to recover edited copies. But normalization alone never proves a clone. The engine also checks the source content, consistent renaming, and which operations are actually being called.
scenes.excerpt: Normalization alone cannot establish a clone.

scenes.title: Reading the categories honestly
scenes.narration: Findings fall into clear categories: identical code, nearly identical copies with renames or small edits, similar code with larger structural edits, and optional embedding-based candidates for same behavior. That last one is a lead, not proof that two implementations are interchangeable. Shape-only matches share layout but negligible content. They are informational, contribute nothing to clone counts or duplication percentages, and never count as clones.
scenes.excerpt: Review both implementations; this is not proof that they are interchangeable.

scenes.title: Ranking by duplicated mass
scenes.narration: Clusters are ranked by duplicated mass: the size of a copied syntax tree multiplied by its additional visible copies. Bigger copies with more duplicates surface first. Mass is a size measure, not a confidence score or a percentage. The duplication percentage separately counts covered source lines, with overlaps counted once. Every verdict can be re-checked by comparing two occurrences directly, and the report stays current as you edit.
scenes.excerpt: Mass is neither confidence nor a percentage.
